title: Cyberstalking - evidence collection tips for victims
p1: A cyberstalker can delete a message in seconds — but the evidence trail may still exist. Many victims lose valuable proof because they react first and document later.
p2: A common misconception is that taking screenshots is always enough. Screenshots can help, but details like dates, usernames, profile links, message history, and the pattern of repeated contact often make the evidence much stronger.
p3: If you experience cyberstalking, avoid engaging with the person and start preserving records early. Save messages, emails, call logs, URLs, and any changes to accounts or profiles. Keep copies in a safe place because online content can disappear or be edited. One overlooked detail: even a deleted post or account activity may leave digital traces that investigators can sometimes verify.
conclusion: Have you ever wondered what information people should save first when dealing with online harassment or cyberstalking?
